hook: The young president of the space race and the Cuban Missile Crisis, killed in Dallas.

pages.x: John Fitzgerald Kennedy was born in 1917 in Brookline, near Boston, the second of nine children of a rich and ambitious family. He was often ill as a boy.

In the Second World War, in 1943, a Japanese destroyer cut his patrol boat in two. He towed an injured sailor for hours, holding a strap of his life jacket in his teeth, to a small island. Help came after he scratched a message on a coconut.

He was elected to Congress, then the Senate. In 1960 he beat Richard Nixon after the first debates shown on television, and at 43 became the youngest person ever elected president, and the first Catholic.

In his first speech as president, in January 1961, he asked Americans to think not about what their country could do for them, but what they could do for it. He started the Peace Corps, sending young volunteers to help abroad.
In April 1961 an invasion of Cuba by exiles, trained by the CIA, collapsed within days. Kennedy took the blame.

In October 1962 American spy planes found Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba. For 13 days the world stood on the edge of nuclear war. Kennedy blockaded the island, and the Soviet leader Khrushchev agreed to take the missiles away.
He set America the goal of landing a man on the Moon before the decade was out. "We choose to go to the Moon," he told a crowd in Texas, because it was hard.
In June 1963, before a huge crowd in West Berlin, he declared in German that he too was a Berliner. A popular myth says he called himself a doughnut. He did not.
On 22 November 1963 he was shot and killed while riding in an open car through Dallas. The man arrested, Lee Harvey Oswald, was himself shot dead two days later.
Kennedy's short presidency, cut off by his murder, inspired a generation with its hope and energy, and set America on its way to the Moon.
pts: Youngest person elected president of the United States
Steered the world through the Cuban Missile Crisis
Set the goal of landing on the Moon
